summary: Approval URL queryparam encoding breaks JIT service token exchange for temporary service accounts
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of just-in-time (JIT) temporary service account provision flows are failing during the approval-token exchange step. The approval URL generated by the approval service includes query parameters that are URL-encoded differently by the identity-proxy edge (percent-encoding vs plus-for-space). The mismatch causes the token exchange to reject the callback, which prevents issuance of short-lived service tokens used by automation runbooks and oncall tooling.

Impact:
- Several oncall runbooks that rely on temporary service accounts cannot complete (blocked actions).
- Affected teams: Platform SRE, CI/CD runners, internal migration tooling.
- Estimated ~12% of JIT flows in us-east fail since 2025-02-10 06:12 UTC.

Environment:
- Deployment: production (api-gateway -> identity-proxy -> svc-provisioner -> auth-service)
- Region: us-east
- Users: internal support tooling, oncall SRE automation, scheduled migration jobs

Steps to reproduce (observed locally and in prod traces):
1. Create a JIT approval request via /internal/approvals API (approval service v2.3.1).
2. Approval service emails/calls back with approval URL: https://console.redwood.internal/approve?token=<base64+urlencoded>
3. Click the approval link; identity-proxy decodes the querystring and forwards to svc-provisioner callback (/cb/approve).
4. svc-provisioner receives decoded token but validation fails with 400 and logs "token signature mismatch".

Observed behavior:
- svc-provisioner rejects the exchange because the token payload differs after the edge re-encoding (space characters encoded as '+' in one place and '%20' in another).
- Identity-proxy access logs show the original incoming querystring includes '+' characters; downstream svc-provisioner logs show '%20' in token content.
- No authenticated session is created; no temporary token issued.

Expected behavior:
- Token in callback should match the approval-token originally issued by approval service (idempotent encoding/decoding across proxies).

Logs / traces (excerpts):
- identity-proxy (2025-02-10T06:17:02Z): "GET /approve?token=eyJhbGciOi...+abc123 HTTP/1.1" 302
- svc-provisioner (2025-02-10T06:17:02Z): "POST /cb/approve - body token=eyJhbGciOi...%20abc123 - validation failed: signature mismatch"
- auth-service (2025-02-10T06:17:03Z): "validation error from svc-provisioner: token payload hash mismatch"

Temporary workaround:
- Manual copy/paste of approval token from email into the svc-provisioner callback UI succeeds (bypasses edge decoding).
- Engineering oncall has a script to re-encode '+' to '%20' prior to exchange for affected runs (not ideal).

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: identity-proxy is normalizing query params using a legacy parser that maps space to '+'.
- Hypothesis B: approval service recently changed token generation to use base64url but left an intermediate step that emits '+' for certain padding sequences.
- Request flow confirmed in packet captures: client -> identity-proxy (unchanged) -> proxy rewrites redirect -> svc-provisioner receives rewritten token.
- Replayed failing requests in staging with both NGINX and identity-proxy reproduce the mismatch only when proxy-level redirect is used.

Immediate action items raised:
- Add validation logging in svc-provisioner to dump raw request querystring vs decoded token hash (low-risk, deployed to staging).
- Reproduce with minimal curl + proxy to isolate whether redirect or querystring parsing transforms token.
- Short-term mitigation: update identity-proxy redirect handler to avoid percent-decoding the token query parameter when the key name is 'token' (patch candidate).

Longer-term considerations:
- Consolidate token encoding to base64url without characters that are ambiguous in querystrings.
- Harden validation to canonicalize token before signature verification (explicit policy).

Attachments / cross refs:
- Slack: #internal-support (thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1676030000000000)
- Incidents: related incident snapshot INT-462199 for a similar token parsing problem in 2024-11 (reference)
comments: 2025-02-10 08:03 - Jamal Reed (assignee): I've reproduced the failing path with a local identity-proxy build. The redirect handler calls decode_querystring() before building the redirect URL. Leaving a note: this looks like a parsing/normalization bug in the edge library (libedge v1.8.0).

2025-02-10 09:45 - Priya Desai (SRE): Temporary mitigation deployed to canary identity-proxy in us-east: add a conditional that preserves raw 'token' param during redirect. Observed failing rate drop to ~1.7% for canary traffic. Rolling more broadly pending validation.

2025-02-11 13:12 - Jamal Reed: Opened PR to change redirect behaviour and added a unit test to ensure '+' isn't converted to '%20' for 'token' param. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1423
2025-02-12 10:02 - Aisha Kapoor: Customer-facing teams informed; added note in #platform-updates that some automation runs may require manual token re-issuance until fix fully rolled out.
investigation_notes: Edge library (libedge) v1.8.0 uses querystring parser built on older urltools that treats '+' as space. Upstream upgrade to urltools v2.0.0 includes strict parsing option.
svc-provisioner validation uses base64url expectations; canonicalization step missing when tokens pass through proxies.
Canary mitigation performed; metrics show a decrease in failures from ~12% -> ~1.7% on canary shard. Need rollout plan and monitoring dashboard update.
next_steps: Merge identity-proxy PR and deploy to us-east within standard change window (owner: Jamal Reed).
Add regression test to CI that asserts token passthrough for redirect flows (owner: Jamal).
Run full canary for 24 hours and monitor token-exchange success rate; if stable promote to 100% (owner: Priya Desai).
Follow-up: schedule a postmortem note linking INT-462199 and update the runbook to include this edge-case (owner: Aisha Kapoor).

notes: This issue touches JIT token exchange security path; coordinate with Security for any changes to token handling policy.
